# NEPTUNI · English · catálogo de piezas: descripciones (1)
mp7g7lq An octagonal cross-shaped structure with the throttleable engine in the center, four tanks in the square bays and equipment in the triangular corner bays. It stayed on the Moon as the launch pad for the ascent stage.
qn9qxns Two pairs of parallel beams with webs at ±27 in, upper and lower decks and closing bulkheads, plus the fittings that join it to the ascent stage. Layout documented; thicknesses reconstructed.
1fiyz71 Multilayer aluminized Kapton blankets (amber, reddish amber, black and silver) and a lower shield against the engine plume. When the stage is opened they move apart to show the inside. The distribution of colors per panel is reconstructed.
qxdzrz8 Two Aerozine 50 tanks and two nitrogen tetroxide tanks in the square bays between the beams, around the engine. The LM structures guide is inconsistent about which pair of bays holds the oxidizer; the tank shape is approximate.
9u3q180 A 9,870 lbf throttleable engine burning hypergolic propellants, with an ablative chamber and a radiation-cooled niobium nozzle. Thrust and gimbal documented; nozzle profile reconstructed.
sv8fhg7 A radiation-cooled niobium extension with a 1.52 m exit diameter. The diameter follows the reference model; the profile curve is inferred.
uh1e31z The engine could tilt up to 6° to follow the center of mass. The gimbal is documented; the shape of the ring and actuators is inferred.
fdrlmkq Pipes running from the four tanks to the throttleable engine's valve assembly. The feed is documented; routing and diameters inferred.
aecdmuq Helium, water and gaseous oxygen tanks and descent batteries in the corner bays. General location documented; exact shape and position inferred.
cx6ak7g Doppler radar and altimeter under the descent stage; it gave altitude and speed to the guidance computer. Shape and position reconstructed.
pmfbgxm A modular storage unit in the forward left compartment, on a fold-down panel that served as a workbench. It held the TV camera, the tripod, the tools, the SWC and the two sample boxes.
qc871lp Two sealed aluminum boxes carried in the MESA: one for the bulk sample and one for the documented samples and the core tubes. At the end of the EVA they were lifted into the cabin with the equipment conveyor (LEC) and came back to Earth with the samples. Dimensions from the sampling tool catalog; layout in the MESA reconstructed.
ionmuzh A two-person pressurized cabin, a midsection with the ascent engine tanks, a docking tunnel and an aft equipment bay. It lifted off from the Moon with Armstrong and Aldrin.
q064nta A thermal and micrometeoroid shield of multilayer Mylar and aluminum skin, set apart from the pressurized cabin, with triangular windows. Faceted shape reconstructed from the NASA model and photographs.
z6vzgz6 A square 32 × 32 in (0.81 m) hatch through which the astronauts crawled out to the porch wearing their suits and PLSS backpacks. It opened inward. The opening direction and the hinge mechanism shown are reconstructions.
snh4rz2 Upper tunnel of ≈ 32 in with the hatch and the probe-and-drogue ring, and a docking target on top of the cabin. Existence and diameters documented; details reconstructed.
mw4k06f The commander's and LM pilot's panels and the central pedestal with the DSKY. Their existence and general layout are documented; the instruments drawn are representative.
efs5dsl The crew's interface with the guidance computer, on the pedestal between the two stations. Existence and function documented; appearance representative.
72vmrla An attitude controller (ACA) for the right hand and a thrust/translation controller (TTCA) for the left at each station, and elastic restraints that held the astronauts while standing. Existence documented; shape and mounting approximate.
a275v2b Cabin floor and the ascent engine cover, which stuck up about 18 in into the midsection. Layout inferred.
3cf7r4d A fixed-thrust hypergolic engine without a gimbal, which fired only once to lift off using the descent stage as a launch pad. It sat recessed in the central cavity of the descent stage. Nozzle shape reconstructed.
8hlhy15 An open frame behind the midsection with ascent stage batteries, environmental control components and gaseous oxygen tanks, covered by thermal blankets. General contents documented; layout reconstructed.
y65rj31 The two PLSS backpacks with their OPS, stowed at the back of the cabin, and the cameras: the 16 mm one in the LM pilot's window and the Hasselblad. Existence documented; positions inferred.
9mm8ssk The layout of Tranquility Base during the EVA: flag, EASEP experiments, solar wind sheet, TV camera on its tripod, tools, LEC conveyor and commemorative package. On the exterior these items appear stowed. Inventory and distances documented; directions reconstructed.
qtmak0m A 3 × 5 ft (0.91 × 1.52 m) nylon flag with a top hem holding a crossbar, so it would look like it was waving in the vacuum. The pole and crossbar were one-inch gold anodized aluminum tubes in two telescoping sections. On Apollo 11 the crossbar didn't fully extend, which left the ripples seen in the photographs. Aldrin set it about 27 ft (8.2 m) from the LM's axis; the pole went only about 7 in into the ground and the liftoff blast knocked it over. Dimensions and distance documented; direction reconstructed.
rw9cr2d A double-walled tube (stainless steel outside, an aluminum layer, Thermoflex insulation and several layers of Kapton) mounted next to the left side of the ladder. It kept the flag below about 82 °C while the engine plume reached ≈ 1,090 °C in the last seconds of the descent. It stayed on the leg. Composition and location documented; dimensions reconstructed.
0suclhu The first seismometer installed on another celestial body. A cylindrical sensor about 23 × 29 cm, with three long-period seismometers and one short-period, under a hat-shaped thermal shield; it was powered by six solar panels in two wings. Aldrin placed it 16.8 m south of the LM, leveled with a ball level and aligned using a gnomon's shadow. It sent data for a few weeks. Dimensions from the Smithsonian qualification model; housing color and antenna reconstructed.
mnkz89j A 45 cm square panel with 100 fused-silica corner reflectors 3.8 cm across, recessed 1.9 cm to protect them. It returns laser pulses fired from Earth and is still used to measure the Earth–Moon distance to within centimeters; it's the only Apollo 11 experiment still working. Aldrin pointed it at Earth with a sun compass, about 18 m from the LM. Dimensions, number of cubes and position documented; base and mount reconstructed.
v92g4zl A 1.40 × 0.30 m aluminum sheet hung from a telescoping mast and turned toward the Sun to catch solar wind ions. Aldrin deployed it before planting the flag; it was exposed for 77 minutes and the sheet came back to Earth to be analyzed at the University of Bern. It was designed by the University of Bern (Switzerland). Dimensions, orientation and stowage in the MESA documented; mast height and position on the ground reconstructed.
youg6oa A black-and-white slow-scan camera that rode in the MESA and broadcast Armstrong's first step as he came down the ladder. Afterwards it was mounted on a tripod away from the LM, connected by a 100 ft cable, for a fixed view of the rest of the EVA. It stayed on the Moon. Existence, cable and abandonment documented; shape, distance and direction of the tripod reconstructed.
l56fxsg A folding tripod, stowed in the MESA (LM-5 stowage list, 1.74 lb), on which the TV camera was mounted for the fixed view of the EVA. Height reconstructed.
v4f0xao A 100 ft (30.5 m) cable connecting the camera to the descent stage. It was left lying on the regolith. Length documented; routing reconstructed.
p99yoe8 A large box-shaped scoop (39 cm), an extension handle, tongs, a hammer, two core tubes with a 2 cm inner diameter and a gnomon. They were used to collect the bulk sample and the documented samples; the tubes were driven in with the hammer. The scoop, tongs, hammer, handle and gnomon stayed on the Moon. Types and dimensions from the tool catalog; their stowage in the MESA appears on the LM-5 list. The inner layout of the MESA and the positions on the ground are reconstructions.
zpussfo A looped strap, like a pulley clothesline, to raise and lower equipment between the hatch and the ground without carrying it down the ladder: that's how the sample boxes and cameras went up. It traveled in a bag in the cabin and was left on the Moon. Existence and use documented; routing reconstructed.
0p9ycwi A small bag left on the ground at the end of the EVA holding the silicon disk with goodwill messages from world leaders, a gold olive branch, the Apollo 1 patch in memory of Grissom, White and Chaffee and two medals honoring Gagarin and Komarov. Contents documented; shape and position next to the ladder reconstructed.
7ibep0c Four cantilevered legs with a crushable honeycomb main strut, secondary struts, 37 in footpads and probes on three of them; the front leg carries the ladder, the porch and the plaque.
cyuijy1 Outer cylinder and inner rod; the aluminum honeycomb cartridge crushes permanently when it takes the load. Diameters reconstructed from the NASA model.
yzpwicp A 37 in (0.94 m) footpad joined to the main strut by a ball joint, so it could adapt to the slope of the ground. The gold covering reproduces the Kapton blankets visible in surface photographs.
h6yttez Support trusses fixed to the body, secondary struts and the deploy-and-lock mechanism. Existence documented; geometry from the NASA model.
ioch6jo A 1.71 m rod hanging below the footpad that lit the «Lunar Contact» light when it touched the ground, the signal to shut down the engine. After landing it was left bent on the ground; the bent shape is a visual reconstruction.
fagwxvp A ladder mounted on the front leg's strut, from the porch down to near the footpad, which Armstrong and Aldrin climbed down to the surface. Number of rungs and spacing reconstructed.
f071840 An outside platform mounted on the front truss, just below the hatch, from which the astronauts backed out toward the ladder. Handrails and dimensions reconstructed.
uyvrhpt A 9 × 7⅝ in stainless steel plaque fixed to the ladder between the third and fourth rungs from the bottom, curved to wrap around the leg without getting in the way. It remains on the Moon with the descent stage. It bears the text «Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon, July 1969 A.D. We came in peace for all mankind», Earth's two hemispheres and the signatures of Armstrong, Collins, Aldrin and Nixon (the hemispheres and signatures are not reproduced here).
y1vgr6n A 26 in steerable S-band antenna, VHF, flight and EVA antennas, and the S-band electronics in the aft bay.
idoy968 A 26 in (0.66 m) dish antenna that carried voice, telemetry and the television signal of the first step to Earth. It could be pointed on two axes.
1kiz4ej A truss extending over the upper right of the midsection and a two-axis mount for pointing at Earth. Location documented; geometry reconstructed.
u0nnsrt S-band transceiver. Existence documented; position in the aft bay and shape inferred.
7ckya1z S-band power amplifier and coaxial cables to the antenna. Existence documented; position, shape and routing inferred.
5gedl9o Two VHF flight antennas for talking to the command module, two S-band flight antennas for the omnidirectional link with Earth and one VHF antenna for extravehicular activity communications. The number of flight antennas is documented; their shape and position are taken from the NASA model.
25k2ozk The LM guidance computer, alignment telescope and rendezvous radar. The radar is visible on top of the cabin; the computer and the telescope are inside the ascent stage.
iu9futt A Block II AGC measuring 24 × 12.5 × 6.5 in and weighing 70 lb. Dimensions and technology documented; the structures guide places it in the midsection and the exact mounting point is inferred.
xgkhpl9 About 2,800 NOR circuits in flat packages soldered to boards, with wire wrap potted in epoxy. The number and layout of the blocks shown are representative, not a drawing of the trays.
bzqiso6 A 36,864-word read-only memory woven from wires that passed through or around ferrite cores. Capacity documented; the number and shape of the modules shown are representative.
lehtn83 A digital computer about 61 × 32 × 17 cm and 32 kg, with about 2,800 NOR-gate integrated circuits in flat packages, soldered to boards, interconnected by wire wrap and then potted in epoxy, 2,048 words of erasable memory and 36,864 of core rope memory. The LM structures guide places it in the midsection; the exact mounting point and internal layout are shown approximately. The DSKY on the console was its interface with the crew.
vba9uc5 A periscope for sighting stars and aligning the guidance system's inertial platform. Position in the cabin roof inferred.
aktsork A two-axis steerable antenna on top of the cabin that tracked the command module's transponder from 80 ft to 400 nautical miles. Function and range documented; shape reconstructed.
c8fge60 Four quads of four 100 lbf thrusters mounted on trusses at the corners of the ascent stage, and deflectors that protected the descent stage from their plumes.
swafia0 One of the four thruster quads mounted on arms at 90° to each other. Each quad has four 100 lbf (445 N) thrusters: two vertical and two horizontal. Two independent feed systems supplied half of the thrusters in each quad. The mount geometry is reconstructed.
3aw3mpx Angled plates that protected the descent stage from the plume of the downward-pointing RCS thrusters. Taken from the NASA model; their exact shape is approximate.
cs9c3ab Explore this mission's own optical system, its detectors, drives and connections.
ih2q7d2 A steerable mirror scanned a vertical line; rotation in azimuth completed the image. Use the rotation control to see the scanning principle.
5wmmrxt The lens had a 0.95 cm aperture and a 5.37 cm focal length. The visible lenses explain the optical path; its exact prescription has not been recovered.
8ut9jtd Lenses and solid rings spread apart to explain the assembly.
2m32smr Twelve channels of photodiodes and filters, not a CCD array that takes an instant photo. Their fine layout in this cutaway is explanatory.
is8f60j Torque actuators, bearings and the angular resolution of the scan. Winding and tooth geometry is illustrative.
ifagxfx Solid copper conductors and the actuator's inner shaft.
wdbepnd Period circuit boards, pins, passives, traces and connection loops. They do not reproduce a public manufacturing netlist.
xmn84v7 The vertical window, the seals and the CO₂ nozzle protect the scanning mechanism.
yya8z27 The 10 cm magnifying mirror and the magnetic target were used to look at samples and check the images. They are science equipment: they don't connect the radio to the antenna.
qjxxxnp A magnifying reflector for looking at material collected by the sampler. The small mount is reconstructed from the diagrams.

yxjjvxx The mechanism collected and positioned samples. This view shows its supports and connections.
kfbicet The boom positioned the collector head in azimuth, elevation and extension. It shows the tube with its lengthwise seam, supports and base mechanism.
zl61pyk The collector head picked up material and could work as a scoop and a small backhoe.
7zbvykv A motor in the rear cylinder flipped the collector head over to deliver samples. The outer geometry follows figure 107 of NASA RP-1027.
ixrgbb6 The sieve in the lid separated material. Its holes are modeled in 3D; the hole pattern is approximate.
txjmz2q The small tool underneath helped with digging; the brush cleaned the magnet assembly.
8hxeyhv The solenoid opened, closed and vibrated the lid. The 1973 study documents 8.8 Hz pulses; no flight operation is simulated.
l8kmimj Instruments on the collector head to investigate magnetic and physical properties.
1klug4y Explanatory cutaway of the drive; the windings, shaft and contacts are modeled in 3D.
mdthwaz Connections and clamps on the boom. The fine routes are reconstructed approximately.
4h40cnm Viking used two SNAP-19 generators: heat from the radioisotope, thermoelectric conversion and cooling fins.
cjfk1hd Plutonium-238 supplied heat inside a capsule with graphite protection. Its inner shape is shown in an explanatory way.
zifco0h Each SNAP-19 had six modules of fifteen thermoelectric pairs. They turned heat into electricity with no moving parts.
nom75ht The six fins belong to the generator's metal radiator. They are not a solar panel.
ll3u9mb Housing, ribbed end caps and a 26-pin connector; its finish represents the radiator alloy.
782tg4v Stitched outer cover and its fasteners; it is removed to reveal the radiator.
zpd14yi Viking's three biology experiments studied soil samples. Their results did not confirm life.
aauaen0 Sample chamber, gas supplies and chromatographic analysis; explanatory internal geometry.
jbt4jh8 Four test cells received samples and labeled nutrients. The chemical result alone did not confirm life.
24zqnpz Incubation and pyrolysis cells, gas supply and carbon measurement.
jbf7nre Restrained ducts and period electronics with passives, contacts and traces; their fine details are explanatory.
0sxwzn6 Opening it separates the cover, boards, power supply and harnesses. The architecture is explained through its known functions; the internal details are not flight CAD.
dvc66f8 Two channels for guidance, control and sequencing. Boards with period packages, axial passives, contacts and explanatory 3D traces.
shnpqih The traces explain connections; not all flight netlists and locations are publicly known.
mkzj676 Each GCSC had 18K 24-bit words of plated-wire memory. The visible grid explains that principle; it is not ferrite-ring memory.
mw4h48g Conversion of RTG power, battery charging and power distribution. An illustrative board of the documented subsystem is shown.
387bcyw Two assemblies held two batteries each: four batteries of 30 V nominal, 24 cells and 8 Ah per battery. They supplied the power peaks. The fine layout of cells and terminals is explanatory.
c2d293g The loops follow the opening between boards, avoiding floating connections that don't move.
7wa5dnp The struts, joints and footpads steadied the spacecraft after landing.
8xbt1ja The impact crushed aluminum honeycomb. It didn't work like a spring that bounces back. The demonstration shows that principle, without computing flight loads.
skuuw8y Hollow aluminum cells that absorb energy by crushing.
e95scbz The three footpads form a triangle about 2.21 m on each side.
d2yqfqu Tie rods, ball joints and load limiters join the supports to the body. The pins and the stroke indicator follow the photographs.
60u9vgi The reflector, feed and radio linked the vehicle with its communication links.
h5k9g3f A 76.2 cm steerable reflector, with a central feed and rear supports. The orientation is a representative pose, not the pointing on a specific sol.
6havhp0 The bent deployable mount and the elevation/azimuth drives pointed the antenna. The nominal mast was 55.88 cm. The rear housings and the fine harness routes are visual reconstructions.
bz86noa Transponder, amplification and control. The PCB illustrates technology of the era, without claiming its exact flight connections.
n23rkvs The coax loop follows the opening and keeps the link between the reflector and the radio.
19mkoaz The UHF link relayed data through the orbiter. Its antenna was on the side between legs 1 and 3, not on top of the RTG cover.
d67flo7 Eight crossed-dipole elements and a ground plane. It sat on the main fitting of leg 3; it wasn't a rod on top of the insulation.
hhd0q22 The open view shows the tanks, chamber, nozzle, valves and feed lines.
9m1mogs Spherical titanium tanks with a 57.9 cm inner diameter. The descent system used slosh and anti-vortex baffles, without a separating diaphragm. The cutaway and the shape of the baffles are educational.
vzyegkc Three variable-thrust engines spread their exhaust through eighteen nozzles to disturb the ground less.
5wk56h6 Two pairs of small engines controlled roll during the descent. Their envelope is reconstructed from figures 72–74.
jfd06k5 Explanatory assembly of the descent feed valves and ports.
pzdnl7e Pipes modeled in 3D with visible fittings; their fine internal routes are approximate.
xbabozp Viking's deployable boom carried hot-film wind sensors and three temperature thermocouples. Explore its supports and connections.
ggj773g Two perpendicular hot-film sensors and a quadrant sensor worked out speed and direction. Three thermocouples measured temperature.
2q1qzxe The boom deployed with a torsion spring and was held by latches.
ovqtnx7 Heating control, signal conditioning and connection of the sensors. Explanatory electronic detail.
0bb9s46 Viking combined three ovens and a GCMS chromatograph/spectrometer with X-ray fluorescence to analyze what the soil was made of. The internal cutaways are explanatory.
a4gu54c Pyrolysis prepared the samples so compounds could be identified in the chromatograph and spectrometer.
hvjiudk Columns and carrier gas flow; the coils show their function, with approximate dimensions.
mgc1os1 Separating and identifying molecules from their masses.
h4pgghm The X-ray fluorescence analysis used four counters and Fe-55 / Cd-109 sources.
dyat5oc Period PCBs, connectors, passives and traces illustrating the electronic control.
mykf3qt The cover is removed step by step so you can tell the analysis groups apart.
zl7x5q9 The warm electronics box (WEB) is the central structure: composite honeycomb panels insulated with aerogel. The equipment deck (RED) closes it on top and holds the mast, three antennas, the calibration targets and the fixed solar panel. Under a front shelf is the arm's stowage space.
xk5s1n4 A thermal enclosure that protects the batteries, electronics and the Mini-TES spectrometer. It combines insulation, waste heat, eight RHUs and electric heaters.
fqxgbtg Composite panels with a gold outer skin. The panel and skin thickness are inferred; the material is documented.
lid0beg Silica aerogel that reduces the WEB's heat loss during the Martian night.
zoyslh8 Cable pass-throughs in the rear wall; number and position inferred.
97fxt4u A C-channel with tabs for the turret's «T», a hook for the elbow and a mount for the pyrotechnic cable cutter that released the arm after landing.
31menfn An 8 × 8 cm sundial with a 6 cm post, gray rings and four color chips. Children's drawings on the sides of the base.
u25v023 Capture and filter magnets at the base of the PMA and a sweep magnet next to the Pancam calibration target. A fourth set is on the RAT.
74yoq6i Bundles visible in flight photographs between the mast, the antennas and the WEB. Approximate routing.
gxwn79d A springless rocker-bogie suspension with a passive differential: each rocker carries the front wheel and a bogie with the middle and rear wheels. The beams are welded, tapered titanium boxes. The suspension folded for launch with three break points and six joints that locked when deployed.
l9nmmsf A front rocker to the front wheel and a rear rocker with a welded «knee» up to the bogie pivot. Tapered box beams, typical wall 1 mm (1.5 mm at the seam).
0echcgm A single-use fork-and-clevis joint on 52 mm Torlon bushings. It locks with a ratchet after turning 39° while the rover stands up.
m86vjii The front rocker's motorized joint: it swung each front wheel 180° from its upside-down stowed position. A 100 mm × Ø80 mm body with a Maxon RE020 motor and a 5-stage planetary gearbox.
xdewyqp Housing for the cross axle that joins each rocker to the body. Its lengthwise position is inferred from the origin of the rover's mechanical frame (29 cm ahead of the middle axle).
kmi7ppw Each bogie shares the load between the middle and rear wheels. The rear section telescopes: the rear wheel extended it 17 cm and locked it in the last step of the deployment.
z6u5ccn A rear section that slides inside the front one on rollers with Belleville washers; the ratchet clicks into a window in the front bogie.
8y6x2ak The passive differential forces the two rockers to turn in opposite directions and sets the body's pitch at the average. The sources confirm a differential with links and a «differential interface» on each rocker; the rear bar and the links shown are an inferred layout.
oi293eu A representative assembly of the four steered corners: steering actuator, strut, drive actuator and wheel.

0hkwjrj A steering actuator above the wheel: a vertical axis through the center of the wheel. The four outer wheels steer independently; the middle ones don't.
6ngj22g A titanium strut running down the inside of the wheel to the drive actuator.
v9vhrpt Each of the six wheels has its own actuator inside the hub. The sources consulted don't publish the winding, gear ratio or gear layout: only the envelope and the interface are shown.
5yes3go A crowned black anodized aluminum rim with crosswise grousers and curved spokes that absorb shocks. Diameter 26.2 cm at the center and 23.2 cm at the edges; 16 cm wide.
cce3q9o The middle wheels don't steer. Their axle lines up with the origin of the MER navigation frame.
pg67ol9 Polyimide-wrapped bundles that follow the beams to the actuators, with service loops at the moving joints. The exact routing is reconstructed from photographs.
svl6eij One fixed panel on top of the RED and five folding wings: the two front ones and the rear one hinged to the deck, and two rear side wings hinged to the front ones. In total 1.3 m² of GaInP/GaAs/Ge triple-junction cells.
n1gyafc Each cell has its own cover glass; there is no continuous sheet over the panel. Thickness not documented.
x9d6qv0 Three stacked photovoltaic layers: gallium indium phosphide, gallium arsenide and germanium. The size and number of cells in this grid are a visual estimate.
4dhyetz Contacts between neighboring cells that form the panel's strings. Representative layout.
2qy99uc Composite panels with a shiny metal underside (the rear Hazcams catch reflections in it). The hinges let the wings fold inside the landing module.
gghj3om The Mini-TES spectrometer sits inside the WEB and uses the hollow mast as a periscope. The head mirror is aimed with the PMA's elevation and can look from +30° to −50°. It is a different instrument from the cameras.
p60r4vk A Michelson interferometer with a ±0.25 mm moving mirror and a 978 nm reference laser. The internal layout is a reconstruction within the documented envelope.
cqfabad A 6.35 cm primary. It is shown looking up the mast's axis (orientation INFERRED).
p2skjd9 Beam splitter, fixed mirror and moving mirror. Geometry INFERRED.
07vo8r4 Uncooled thermal detector; position inferred.
95xwema The instrument's electronics; educational layout with no invented traces.
pwumuby A 23.5 × 16.3 × 15.5 cm envelope.
f5lhgmm Located 10.7 cm to the right of the PMA head's axis (NAIF). It turns with the PMA's elevation.
rjgs750 Educational diagram: radiation enters through the head mirror, travels down the hollow mast and reaches the telescope. It's a diagram, not a part.
2wem7v6 One external target on the deck, with grooves 1.73 mm deep and 1.2 mm apart, and another internal one in the mast assembly.
u0kf5sk The mast lifts the cameras to 1.54 m. On the bar are the two science Pancams at the ends (30 cm baseline, 1° toe-in) and the two engineering Navcams in the middle (20 cm baseline). The mast turns 370° in azimuth and the bar 194° in elevation.
dtj5n99 A fixed-focus lens (hyperfocal at 3 m) with discrete spherical elements. It has no zoom. The internal position of each lens is an educational representation.
rdlgppx Each Pancam has an 8-position wheel with 11 mm interference filters. L1 is empty; 13 filters are for geology and 2 for the Sun. «Turn filters» moves it one position (45°).
dx8g0et A 1024 × 2048-pixel frame-transfer CCD (1024 × 1024 active) and an electronics box shared by the rover's nine cameras.
4tp28w7 A short sunshade and internal baffles against stray light.
jq1jqyb Engineering cameras with a 650 nm red filter, used to plan drives and for autonomous navigation.
icdw8rh An aligned titanium mount that carries the four cameras on the elevation head.
l7ma4af Elevation actuator. Its axis is 1.38 m above the ground; the cameras sit 15 cm higher.
5oxjve4 A hollow tube that works as Mini-TES's periscope. It traveled folded on the deck and was raised after landing.
nvus8t5 Helical wiring that follows the azimuth rotation, and the cameras' flex circuits.
1lsxwlh A five-degree-of-freedom arm: shoulder azimuth and elevation, elbow, wrist and turret. It places the microscope, the two spectrometers and the RAT on rocks and soil. It travels folded under a front shelf. This stowed pose is a reconstruction consistent with the documented volume.
aonjdm8 Brushed DC motors with a magnetoresistive encoder. All start with 3 planetary stages; the shoulder and elbow add a harmonic drive, the wrist and turret two more planetary stages.
gi039p9 Elbow cutaway based on figure 5 of the IPS paper. The order of the components is documented; their dimensions are inferred.
61jdbch Titanium housing and shafts to match the thermal shrinkage of the bearings and gears.
e9vndgs A brushed DC motor, a 2-channel encoder and a 4-position magnetic brake.
bqrmr65 A reduction shared by all five joints. The ratio is not published.
y5sanqd A cup-type harmonic gear with S-shaped teeth: a circular spline and a flex-spline.
iy1d4xr A potentiometer for absolute position and a Teflon O-ring against dust.
jvvryde It protects the flex cable loop that runs through the joint.
4q0nckd More than 200 conductors in continuous flex strips about 3 m long, with service loops at each joint.
elrdz6r A brush on the forearm for cleaning the grinding heads. Approximate position.
cid4haj Four tools around the turret axis, with orientations from NAIF: MI 0°, RAT 90°, Mössbauer 190°, APXS 270°.
d6kme1h A fixed-focus camera: the arm is its focusing mechanism. It has a motorized Kapton cover and a spring-loaded contact sensor. It has no zoom.
jrjk382 A probe with a coil spring that can bend 90° and finds small spots accurately.
ub7x5ks A cylindrical head with curium-244 alpha sources and a silicon drift detector in a coaxial layout. Its doors open when it's pressed against a surface; inside is a gold target on Kapton. It is not Sojourner's deployable APXS.
m9fbakm Coaxial layout documented; the number of sources is inferred.
cq5h2q6 Documented components in an inferred layout.
j8g8ab2 A wheel with two diamond-resin heads spins at ≈3,000 rpm while slowly tracing a circle. That way it opens a 45 mm area up to 5 mm deep. It also brushes and carries magnets. It doesn't drill or take cores.
ll91cxu Two curved 6.35 mm heads at the ends of a bar; they trace a 23.37 mm circle.
n3h8wg0 They sweep away the grinding debris.
00dcj6k They collect magnetic dust from the ground rocks.
93pcprq Inside the WEB are the electronics module (REM), two lithium-ion batteries, the IMU and eight RHUs. The radio electronics are mounted on the sides of the REM. The functions are documented; the layout of cards and components is inferred.
1utldux A computer based on the RAD6000, a radiation-hardened version of the PowerPC. This card and its position are an educational representation, not the flight circuit.
dqk6tvx Period ceramic packages. Their number and position do not reproduce the flight board.
g2yq3cx 128 MB of RAM and 256 MB of flash, plus smaller non-volatile memory.
pd4bqhi The motor control card closes the loops with encoders and potentiometers (cited for the IDD).
ny9citr It regulates the power from the panels and controls battery charging. Regulation is not in the panels.
cxi3cql Two rechargeable 8 A·h batteries. They must be above −20 °C to discharge and above 0 °C to charge. The internal cells are not modeled.
4pus8kw Eight ≈1 W RHUs, the size of a C battery. They only provide heat, not electricity: the MER rovers got their electricity from the solar panels. The location of the heaters in the model is approximate.
9lq7zk6 IMU mounted on the REM according to DESCANSO figure 7-14.
